script:
HOW LONG FOOD KEEPS IN A FRIDGE

Milk keeps for about five days after you open it.

Cooked rice keeps for one day only. Cool it fast and put it in the fridge.

Hard cheese keeps for three weeks. Soft cheese keeps for one week.

Eggs do not go in the fridge door. The door is the warmest part.

A fridge should be at five degrees or colder.

items.stem: How long does opened milk keep?
items.rationale: The first line gives about five days for milk once it has been opened, which is shorter than cheese and longer than rice.

items.stem: Which food keeps for the shortest time?
items.rationale: Cooked rice is given one day only, which is less than the milk, the soft cheese and the hard cheese.

items.stem: Why should eggs not go in the door?
items.rationale: The note says the door is the warmest part of the fridge, which is why eggs are kept elsewhere.

items.stem: How cold should a fridge be?
items.rationale: The last line gives five degrees or colder as the temperature a fridge should run at.

script:
CITY BIKES

There are 40 stations in the city. Every station is open all day and all night.

The first 30 minutes are free. After that you pay by the hour.

You need the app. There is no card reader on the bike.

The bikes are green. The blue ones are electric and cost more.

You can leave a bike at any station, not only the one you took it from.

items.stem: How many stations are there?
items.rationale: The first line gives forty stations; thirty is the number of free minutes, which is a different figure.

items.stem: What is free?
items.rationale: The first thirty minutes cost nothing, and time after that is paid by the hour.

items.stem: What do the blue bikes have?
items.rationale: The blue bikes are described as electric, which is why they cost more than the green ones.

items.stem: Where can you leave a bike?
items.rationale: The last line says a bike may be left at any station, not only the one it came from.

script:
THE TOWN MUSEUM

The museum is 100 years old this year.

It is open from Wednesday to Sunday. It is closed on Monday and Tuesday.

Entry is free on the first Sunday of the month. On other days it costs six pounds.

There are three floors. The top floor is about the river.

Bags go in the lockers by the door. The lockers are free.

items.stem: When is the museum closed?
items.rationale: It opens from Wednesday to Sunday, so Monday and Tuesday are the two closed days.

items.stem: When is entry free?
items.rationale: Entry costs nothing on the first Sunday of each month and six pounds on other open days.

items.stem: What is on the top floor?
items.rationale: Of the three floors, the top one is described as being about the river.

items.stem: What do the lockers cost?
items.rationale: Bags go in the lockers by the door, and the note says the lockers are free.

script:
BORROWING E-BOOKS FROM THE LIBRARY

Members can borrow six e-books at a time. A loan lasts twenty-one days and then ends automatically, so nothing is ever returned late and there are no charges.

The library buys a fixed number of copies of each title. If every copy is out, you join a queue. The average wait is eleven days, though a popular title can take much longer.

You can return a book early, and doing so passes it to the next person in the queue immediately.

Audiobooks work in the same way, but they count separately: six e-books and six audiobooks, not six in total.

The app works without a signal once a book has been downloaded.

items.stem: How long is a loan?
items.rationale: A loan runs for twenty-one days and then closes by itself, which is why nothing is returned late.

items.stem: Why are there no late charges?
items.rationale: The loan ends automatically at the end of the period, so a book cannot be kept beyond it.

items.stem: What happens if all copies are out?
items.rationale: The library holds a fixed number of copies, and readers queue when they are all lent out.

items.stem: How many items can a member have?
items.rationale: Audiobooks are counted separately, so a member may hold six e-books and six audiobooks.

items.stem: What does returning a book early do?
options: It shortens the queue at once
It adds a day to the next loan
items.rationale: An early return passes the copy straight to the next person waiting.

script:
WATER AT HOME

An average bath holds about eighty litres. A shower delivers roughly nine litres a minute, so nine minutes matches a bath.

A power shower is different. It can deliver fifteen litres a minute, which means a long one uses more than a bath holds.

A dripping tap wastes five thousand litres a year. The washer inside usually costs less than a pound.

About a third of household water is flushed away. Older toilets use nine litres, although newer ones manage on four or six.

Garden watering is a small part of the year, but a large part of a summer week.

items.stem: How long can a shower run before it matches a bath?
items.rationale: At nine litres a minute, nine minutes of showering reaches the eighty litres an average bath holds.

items.stem: What is different about a power shower?
items.rationale: A power shower can use fifteen litres a minute, so a long one passes the water a bath holds.

items.stem: What does the passage say about a dripping tap?
items.rationale: The washer inside usually costs under a pound, against about five thousand litres wasted a year.

items.stem: How much household water goes down the toilet?
items.rationale: Roughly a third of what a household uses is flushed, whatever the age of the toilet.

items.stem: What does the passage say about garden watering?
items.rationale: Over a whole year it is small, but in a summer week it becomes a large share.

script:
BICYCLES LEFT AT THE STATION

The racks outside the station are free and nobody books a space. Cycles may be left for up to seven days.

Every Tuesday a member of staff marks the wheel of any cycle that has not moved. If the mark is still there the following Tuesday, the cycle is counted as abandoned.

Abandoned cycles are removed to the depot on Wetherby Road and kept for a further month. The owner pays nothing to collect one, but must describe it before it is handed over.

After that month the cycles are given to a workshop that repairs them and passes them to a local charity.

A cycle with a lock cut by staff is photographed first, and the photograph is kept with the record.

items.stem: How long may a cycle be left?
items.rationale: The racks allow up to seven days, after which the marking process begins.

items.stem: How does the station find abandoned cycles?
options: By marking a wheel each Tuesday
items.rationale: A wheel is marked on a Tuesday, and a mark still there a week later means the cycle has not moved.

items.stem: What must an owner do to get a cycle back?
items.rationale: Collection costs nothing, but the owner has to describe the cycle before it is handed over.

items.stem: What happens after the month at the depot?
options: They go to a repair workshop
They are returned to the racks
items.rationale: They pass to a workshop that repairs them and then to a local charity.

items.stem: Why is a photograph taken?
items.rationale: A cycle whose lock is cut is photographed, and that photograph is filed with the record of the removal.
